newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bearish mood persists in East European markets.
newsitem.headline: Bearish mood persists in East European markets.

text.p: Bearish sentiment gripped most East European bourses this week, with shares easing in Prague, Budapest, Ljubliana and Bucharest.
Bratislava bucked the trend with the SAX at a year-high on Friday, while Zagreb shares rallied after mixed trading during the week and small-caps stocks led a rebound in Warsaw.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which reflects price movements in 73 Polish, Czeck, Hungarian, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, fell 3.4 percent this week to close at 1,612.88 points.
PRAGUE
Czech shares continued to plunge throughout the week with the three most heavily capitalised shares -- SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- applying most of the downward pressure.
The three issues, which take 45 percent of the PX50's total capitalisation, fell on average by five percent despite Friday's moderate rebound. The PX50 index dipped 4.2 percent on the week.

Dealers blamed the decline on bearish sentiment in the region but said that the strength of the downturn in Prague was probably due to the high volatility of the Czech crown and profit-taking following strong gains earlier in the year.
WARSAW

Second-tier stocks led the Warsaw bourse's rebound this week but analysts saw their rapid growth leading to equally strong falls, which could pull the market into a fresh round of profit-taking next week.
The main WIG index rose 0.9 percent to 17,704 points this week.
Analysts said a bearish performance of large issues signalled lack of institutional demand, possibly because funds saw Warsaw blue-chips pricey compared with the overall market.
They said small stocks were unlikely to carry the market much further as individual players, who tend to focus on such shares, would be tempted to take quick profits.
BUDAPEST

A bearish mood depressed Hungarian shares on Friday after mixed trading during the week. Turnover was modest as the exchange had little help from the strong dollar and a rising trend on the foreign markets.
On Friday the BUX index closed at 5,381.15 points, down 1.5 points from last Friday's close.

Traders said investors were in a wait-and-see attitude, either sitting on the shares they had bought earlier this year, or looking forward to new issues, like that in oil company MOL or pharmaceuticals company Richter.
BRATISLAVA
A bullish mood gathered pace through the week on the Bratislava Stock Exchange, with the SAX index hitting a year-high of 205.98 on Friday, or 0.82 points up in the week.
Brokers said the bourse, which has been on a gradual uptrend for most of 1997 as foreign investors boosted prices, has not overheated and many issues still offered good value.
Steel maker VSZ remained the most liquid listed issue, closing at 730 crowns on Friday, up 20 for the week.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 3.73 percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index dropped 53.35 points to 1,377.7.
Health resort operator Terme Catez was the leading decliner, while the biggest gainer was brokerage Primofin.
BUCHAREST
Increased volatility of the leu currency with foreign exchange market liberalisation affected Bucharest bourse trading this week with most stocks down in selling pressure.
Investors said they expected a stabilisation of the leu, which weaken slightly against the dollar after a rally earlier in the week, in order to invest again in the bourse.
First-tier Azomures SA fertiliser maker and Oltchim SA chemical plant fell some 6.2 percent and 13.8 respectively to close at 1,530 lei and 1,500.
ZAGREB
After mixed trading for most of the week, Croatian stocks ended up-beat on Friday, led by Zagrebacka Banka's strong recovery. Traders predicted a period of further growth for the main issues.
Zagrebacka, leading commercial bank, gained 140 kuna to close at 1,870 -- 40 kuna off its all time high -- on high volume of 3,203 shares.
Pliva gained five kuna to 470 on volume of 2,788 and Podravka, singled out as "the best buy" by some traders, closed 4.9 kuna lower at 300.
